directAnswer: To reset a Git branch, use the command 'git reset --hard <commit>' to move the branch pointer to a specific commit, discarding all changes after that commit.
summary: This guide provides steps to reset a Git branch, along with potential caveats and frequently asked questions.

sections.heading: Understanding Git Reset
sections.body: The 'git reset' command changes the current branch head to the specified state. It can be used to discard commits, changes in the staging area, or both.

sections.heading: Types of Reset
sections.body: 'git reset' has three main modes: --soft (keeps changes staged), --mixed (keeps changes unstaged), and --hard (discards all changes). Choose the mode based on your needs.

sections.heading: When to Use Reset
sections.body: Use 'git reset' when you want to undo commits or changes in your working directory. Be cautious as it can lead to data loss if used improperly.

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.detail: Launch your terminal or command prompt.

steps.title: Navigate to Repository
steps.detail: Use 'cd <repository-path>' to navigate to your Git repository.

steps.title: Identify Commit
steps.detail: Find the commit hash you want to reset to by using 'git log'.

steps.title: Execute Reset Command
steps.detail: Run 'git reset --hard <commit-hash>' to reset the branch to the specified commit.

faqs.question: What happens to uncommitted changes after a hard reset?
faqs.answer: All uncommitted changes will be lost after a hard reset.

faqs.question: Can I recover lost commits after a reset?
faqs.answer: You can recover lost commits using 'git reflog' to find the commit hash and then reset back to it.

faqs.question: Is there a way to reset without losing changes?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can use 'git reset --soft <commit>' to keep changes staged or 'git reset --mixed <commit>' to keep changes unstaged.

caveats: Using 'git reset --hard' will permanently delete changes in your working directory that are not committed.
Make sure to back up any important changes before performing a reset.
